rows.reason: consumeIdle (host.ts:1201-1254) awaits platform.sessions.readSession (1206), platform.messages.readInbox (1221) and platform.messages.readOutbox (1240) with no local try/catch. Those ports are trackedCall wrappers that do not catch (create-platform.ts:1135-1141, 1251, 1379-1380). readSession awaits records.readMany with no catch (session-directory.ts:1188-1189), and the production SQLite backend's readMany rethrows any BEGIN/work/COMMIT failure (sqlite-record-store.ts:810-818, 287-304). A real ledger I/O/store failure therefore rejects consumeIdle and executes the retry callback at host.ts:1463, which leaves the message pending for the next heartbeat. That is an external store fault, so F; Claude's open question is settled by the unguarded readMany.
rows.proposal: Public steps: start a real Host with an inputConsumers entry plus its matching Query profile, create/activate the Session, send a plain input, then make the Session/inbox read fail. The Host's storage option accepts only kind/directory (host.ts:321-323), so the existing delegating RecordStore wrapper (tests/work-graph/S2B-activity-read-faults.test.ts:30-46) cannot be injected as-is: extend that wrapper to throw and add a narrow Host storage-fault seam (or inject a real ledger I/O error), then clear the fault and assert the same message is consumed on the next heartbeat. Belongs in tests/app/AG2-consultation.test.ts near the real-Host inputConsumers case at 274.

rows.reason: The attention IIFE (host.ts:1443-1446) calls createAttentionObserver(scope.config) at host.ts:1447 for every configured scope before any of the loop's local catches. createAttentionObserver calls validateAttentionConfig (attention-observer.ts:432-433), which throws for heartbeatMs 0 or maxCoalesceMs < heartbeatMs (attention-observer.ts:173-187). Startup validates only pathsKind and trailing slashes (host.ts:1159-1166), and the CLI accepts any attention array (main.ts:170), so a Host started with attention: [{ ... config: { heartbeatMs: 0 } }] gets an already-rejected attentionDone; its only handler is the close-time catch at host.ts:1622, and until close it is an unhandled rejection. Reachable through public configuration without any fault, so G; the unhandled rejection is a real production defect. Codex's D2 misses the creation throw that sits outside the per-operation catches.
rows.proposal: Start the real Host through the AG2b fixture with hostOptions.attention whose config.heartbeatMs is 0 (tests/app/orchestration-mechanism.test.ts:337-339), trap unhandledRejection, close and assert the close-time catch handles it. Better: validate every scope.config with validateAttentionConfig in the host.ts:1159 startup loop and test that the Host refuses at creation; after that fix this catch only guards programming errors and can go (D2).
